headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks from content-writing feeding OCR/browser processing; no direct shared-channel evidence, so pairwise risk is inferred.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing resource with prompt-engineering material, while agent B can run browsers and process documents/images. If A’s outputs are copied into B’s inputs, B may treat attacker-shaped text as instructions. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed, and uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF A’s generated text is pasted into B’s browser or document pipeline
IF B parses document text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to A outputs before handoff
Disable instruction-following on B for untrusted document text
Use a manual review step before B processes A-generated content
requires-engineering: isolate A and B with separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no declared data classes and has no I/O surfaces, while B processes documents/images and has allowlisted network egress. The pair does not show a shared workspace or secrets, so leakage is not evidenced. The main risk is limited to accidental inclusion of sensitive document content in B’s outputs or uploads.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are fed into B
IF B uploads extracted content to an external allowlisted service
mitigations: Restrict B to non-sensitive sample files
Review B’s outbound destinations before use
Redact documents before OCR
Log and inspect one test run end-to-end

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write, network, or concurrency capabilities, so it cannot materially conflict with B’s allowlisted egress and browser use. The pair lacks overlapping mutable-resource writes, git state, or shared OAuth scopes. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF B is configured to modify shared state while A also writes to it
mitigations: Keep A read-only
Assign B a separate workspace
Avoid shared mutable directories
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing agent, so its outputs can become inputs to B’s OCR/document-processing flow. B’s browser and API access make downstream action-taking plausible if it trusts A’s text or extracted facts without verification. No direct evidence shows this happens by default, so the risk is inferred, but the pathway is realistic.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s generated text as authoritative input
IF B acts on extracted claims without a verification step
mitigations: Require B to cite source passages before acting
Insert a human approval step for B outputs
Compare A output against original documents
Use a checksum or provenance tag on handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source content-writing resource with no declared data classes, while B processes documents/images and may egress over allowlisted network paths. No residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to accidental handling of sensitive documents in B. The other agent is not cited because it has no declared compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by B
IF B’s allowlisted egress reaches a non-compliant destination
mitigations: Classify input documents before OCR
Block regulated files from B
Review retention settings for B outputs
Document allowed destinations for B egress
